title: Beluga Liner (Elite Dangerous)
intro: The Beluga Liner by Saud Kruger is a large passenger liner flown from a bridge with multicrew seats and a fighter pilot seat. It needs a large landing pad and uses the shared HOTAS layout.

panels.name: Beluga Liner: seats and hardpoints
panels.text: Facts about the Beluga Liner that set it apart from the other ships: its seats, its weapon mounts and the landing pad size it needs.
panels.context: Everything else in the Beluga Liner's cockpit works like in every other Elite Dangerous ship.

controls.name: Pilot seat (helm)
controls.text: The pilot's seat of the Beluga Liner, the helm. Whoever sits here flies the ship and has the whole HOTAS layout of this guide.
controls.context: The Beluga Liner takes up to four people in all; the other seats are for crew who join in multicrew.

controls.name: Multicrew seats
controls.text: The extra seats of the Beluga Liner, for up to four crew in all. A friend who joins can sit here as gunner, or as fighter controller when the ship carries a fighter.
controls.context: A gunner works the turreted weapons while the pilot flies; the roles are chosen on the role panel.

controls.name: Fighter pilot seat
controls.text: The seat from which a crew member or a hired pilot flies the small fighter that the Beluga Liner can carry in a hangar.
controls.context: The fighter is launched and given orders on the role panel; the preset has no HOTAS button for that.

controls.name: Hardpoints (weapon mounts)
controls.text: The weapon mounts of the Beluga Liner: five medium hardpoints. Bigger mounts take bigger, stronger weapons.
controls.context: The pilot puts the Beluga Liner's weapons into fire groups on the right panel and fires them with the trigger and the weapon release button.

controls.name: Landing pad size
controls.text: The Beluga Liner needs a large landing pad or a bigger one. Stations have small, medium and large pads, and small outposts may not have the bigger ones.
controls.context: When the pilot asks a station for docking, the station gives a pad that fits the ship's size.
